{{< pagebreak >}}

Construction of epidemics
=========================
Parameters
----------
Since we shall only use artificial examples,
we do not define the rate parameters.
```{julia}
const duration = 5.0;
const initial  = SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0);
```

Construction of unconditioned epidemic
--------------------------------------
Here is an `Innovation` to generate the `Evolution` of the unconditioned epidemic:
```{julia}
A = AbstractInfection; I = Infection; P = PInfection; R = Removal; C = CRemoval;
infections = I[I(2t-1, t, t+1) for t in [1,2]] ∪ A[I(0,3,4), I(2,4,5)]
uremovals  = R[R(2t, t) for t in [1,2]] ∪ [R(1,5), R(3,5), R(4,5)]

uiv1 = Innovation(initial.n, infections, uremovals)
```
The `Evolution` of an (_unconditioned_) epidemic is given by:
```{julia}
uev1 = Evolution(initial, uiv1)
```

Construction of conditioned epidemic
------------------------------------
Here is an `Innovation` to generate the `CEvolution` of the corresponding conditioned epidemic:
```{julia}
removals   = R[R(1,5), R(3,5), R(4,5)]
cremovals  = C[C(2t, t) for t in [1,2]] 

iv1 = Innovation(initial.n, infections, removals, cremovals)
```
The `CEvolution` of an (_conditioned_) epidemic is given by:
```{julia}
ev1 = CEvolution(initial, iv1)
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

Tabular and graphical displays of epidemics
===========================================
We first import from `EpidemicsUtilities` some constants 
used for the plotting parameter `select`.
```{julia}
import EpidemicsUtilities: TOP, BOUNDARIES, REGIONS, INFECTIONS, REMOVALS, CREMOVALS, 
    ACTIVATED, ELEMENTS, BASIC, ALL 
```

Table of evolution of epidemic
------------------------------
```{julia}
#| echo: false 
uflow = table_trajectories1(duration, uev1.trajectory) ;
header = [:t, :susceptibles, :infectives, :removals, :epidemic]
Markdown.parse(pretty_table(String, uflow[:,header], 
  header=header, tf=tf_markdown, alignment=[:l, :c, :c, :c, :c]))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
curves_template = plot(uflow, yintercept=1:initial.n,
    Geom.hline(style=:dash, size=0.1mm, color=theme.scaffold),
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=initial.n + 0.25),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    style(default_color=theme.background),
    gadfly_theme) ;

push!(curves_template, layer(uflow, x=:t, y=:empty, Geom.line,
    style(line_width=2theme.trail, default_color=theme.scaffold))) ;

incidents_template = new_figure(curves_template,
    Scale.y_continuous(labels=(initial.n ≤ EpidemicsUtilities.MAXPOP ?
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_circled(i; n=initial.n) :
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_bracketed(i; n=initial.n))),
    Guide.yticks(ticks=collect(1:(initial.n))),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines")) ;

figure_zones = draw_regions!(deepcopy(incidents_template), duration, uflow,
    uev1, theme=theme, select=BOUNDARIES | REGIONS)
depict("test-01-unconditioned", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(figure_zones), uev1, theme=theme, select=BASIC),
        title="Evolution of unconditioned epidemic")
) ;

depict("test-01-conditioned", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(figure_zones), ev1, theme=theme, select=BASIC),
        title="Evolution of conditioned epidemic")
) ;
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

Single step in algorithmic time
===============================

We introduce a new ("candidate")
`Innovation` to be used to derive a single step in algorithmic time
of the entire `CEvolution` trajectory.
```{julia}
infections2c = A[I(1.2,1,2), I(1.3,3,4), I(1.5,2,3), I(3.2,3,4), I(3.6,4,5), I(3.9,4,5)] 
removals2c   = R[R(0.5,2), R(2,3), R(2.3,4), R(3.3,1), R(4.5,5), R(4.8,1)]
cremovals2c  = C[C(2, 2), C(4,5)]

iv2c = Innovation(initial.n, infections2c, removals2c, cremovals2c)
```
Here are figures comparing the candidate innovation for step \(1\)
(@fig-test-02-candidate) and the conditional epidemic evolution at step \(0\)
(@fig-test-02-conditioned, same as @fig-test-01-conditioned).
```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-02-candidate", new_figure(
    draw_innovation!(deepcopy(incidents_template), iv2c, theme=theme, select=ELEMENTS),
        title="Candidate innovation")
) ;
```


::: {#fig-test-02-innov layout-ncol=2}

![Candidate innovation for step 1](image/test-02-candidate.pdf){#fig-test-02-candidate}

![Conditioned evolution, step 0](image/test-01-conditioned.pdf){#fig-test-02-conditioned}

Candidate innovation and current evolution of epidemic.

:::


{{< pagebreak >}}

Substitution of appropriate inactivated removals
------------------------------------------------
The first step is to create a new `Innovation` which 

(a) removes _all_ old unconditioned
`Removal`s and 
(b) inserts those new `Removal`s which remain inactivated.
```{julia}
iv2_1 = Innovation(initial.n, ev1.infections, R[], ev1.cremovals)
ev2_1 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_1)
iv2_2 = Innovation(initial.n, ev2_1.infections, 
    EpidemicsCFTP.inactive_removals(ev1, iv2c), ev2_1.cremovals)
ev2_2 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_2)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-03-removals1", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(figure_zones), ev2_1, theme=theme, select=BASIC),
        title="Old removals removed")
) ;
depict("test-03-removals2", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(figure_zones), ev2_2, theme=theme, select=BASIC),
        title="New inactive removals inserted")
) ;
```


::: {#fig-test-03-removals layout-ncol=2}

![Conditioned evolution, step 2a](image/test-03-removals1.pdf){#test-03-removals1}

![Conditioned evolution, step 2b](image/test-03-removals2.pdf){#test-03-removals2}

Modifying inactivated removal structure

:::

Modifying conditional removal structure
---------------------------------------

The next step is to substitute only those `CRemoval`s which remain activated, while continuing
to use the old `Infection`s
(@fig-test-04-cremovals1 shows relevant `Innovation`, @fig-test-04-cremovals2 shows `CEvolution`).
```{julia}
iv2_3 = Innovation(initial.n, ev2_2.infections, ev2_2.removals, 
    EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev1, iv2c))
ev2_3 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_3)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-04-cremovals1", new_figure(
    draw_innovation!(deepcopy(incidents_template), iv2_3, theme=theme, select=ELEMENTS),
        title="Innovation up to new CRemovals")
) ;
depict("test-04-cremovals2", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(figure_zones), ev2_3, theme=theme, select=BASIC),
        title="Resulting evolution")
) ;
```


::: {#fig-test-04-cremovals layout-ncol=2}

![Innovation with modified removals](image/test-04-cremovals1.pdf){#fig-test-04-cremovals1}

![Resulting conditioned evolution](image/test-04-cremovals2.pdf){#fig-test-04-cremovals2}

Modifying conditional removal structure

:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

Unit tests
==========
The following unit tests should eventually be incorporated in `EpidemicsCFTP/test`
test files.

Unconditioned and conditioned version of `AbstractEvolution`
------------------------------------------------------------
These tests are intended to check that fields are filled correctly.
```{julia}
begin
    A = AbstractInfection; I = Infection; P = PInfection; R = Removal; C = CRemoval;

    @testset "EpidemicsCFTP: $(rpad(Evolution, 23))" begin
        infections = A[I(2t-1, t, t+1) for t in [1,2]] ∪ A[I(0,3,4), I(2,4,5)]
        uremovals  =  [R(2t, t) for t in [1,2]] ∪ [R(1,5), R(3,5), R(4,5)]
        trajectory =  [SIR(0,4,1,0), SIR(1,3,2,0), SIR(2,3,1,1), SIR(3,2,2,1), SIR(4,2,1,2)]
        uiv1 = Innovation(initial.n, infections, uremovals)
        uev1 = Evolution(initial, uiv1)
        history    =  [I(1,1,2), R(2,1), I(3,2,3), R(4,2)]
        @test uev1.infections == sort(infections, lt=isearlier)
        @test uev1.removals   == sort(uremovals,  lt=isearlier)
        @test uev1.chronology == sort(infections ∪ uremovals, lt=isearlier)
        @test uev1.trajectory == trajectory
        @test uev1.history    == history
    end

    removals   =  [R(1,5), R(3,5), R(4,5)]
    cremovals  =  [C(2t, t) for t in [1,2]] 
    @testset "EpidemicsCFTP: $(rpad(CEvolution, 23))" begin
        infections = A[I(2t-1, t, t+1) for t in [1,2]] ∪ A[I(0,3,4), I(2,4,5)]
        trajectory =  [SIR(0,4,1,0), SIR(1,3,2,0), SIR(2,3,1,1), SIR(3,2,2,1), SIR(4,2,1,2)]
        iv1 = Innovation(initial.n, infections, removals, cremovals)
        ev1 = CEvolution(initial, iv1)
        history    = [I(1,1,2), C(2,1), I(3,2,3), C(4,2)]
        @test ev1.infections == sort(infections, lt=isearlier)
        @test ev1.removals   == sort(removals,   lt=isearlier)
        @test ev1.chronology == sort(infections ∪ removals ∪ cremovals, lt=isearlier)
        @test ev1.trajectory == trajectory
        @test ev1.history    == history
    end ;
end ;
```
